2. On 12.07.86 the opposite party No. 1 Agrani Bank, Khatoonganj Branch at Chittagong instituted the above money suit against opposite party No. 2, Bibhuti Bhusan Talukdar and 5 others for a decree for about Taka four crores. 

 4. On 03.03.87 the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted Money Suit No. 06 of 1987 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge at Chittagong against the same opposite party No. 2 for a money decree for Taka 58,08.215. On 31.05.89 the suit was decreed by the Subordinate Judge, First Court. Against the decree, an appeal being First Appeal No. 30 of 1989 subsequently renumbered as First Appeal No. 49 of 1990 was presented by opposite party NO. 2 in this Division and the appeal was dismissed on contest on 09.07.96. 

 5. After the decree was passed, the petitioner already started an execution being Money Execution No. 05 of 1989 against opposite party No. 2 for realisation of decreetal amount of Taka 58,28,481. On the prayer of the petitioner, the Subordinate Judge, First Court by his order dated 22.07.89 passed in Money Execution. Case No. 05 of 1989 attached the sale proceeds of the goods of opposite party No. 2 kept in fixed deposit amounting Taka 92,83182.20 already attached and held by the Commercial Court No. 1 in Money Suit No. 91 of 1986. A copy of the order was also directed to send to the said Commercial Court for taking necessary steps. .By his order dated 15.03.97 the Subordinate Judge, First Court again requested the Commercial Court. No. 1 to take steps in spirit of his order dated 22.07.89. 

 6. On further prayer of the petitioner dated 25.03.97, the Subordinate Judge, First Court wrote a letter to the said Commercial Court requesting him to remit the decreetal amount of Taka 58,08,215 out of the fixed deposit of the Sonali Bank vide memo. No. 66 dated 08.03.98. Thereupon, the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1 considered the purport of the letter as well as the records of the case and held that the request made in the letter could not be carried out in view of the direction of this Division dated 30.06.93 and accordingly, directed to keep the letter in the record of the suit. 

 7. Being aggrieved by the said order, the petitioner obtained the above Rule as stated earlier. Mr. Mahbub Ali appearing on behalf of the petitioner read the provisions of Order XXI Rule 52 of the Code of Civil Procedure, in brief the Code, and submitted that the Commercial Court was obliged to carry out the request of and to remit the decreetal amount to the First Court of Subordinate Judge. Failure of the Commercial Court in remitting the decreetal amount to the First Court of Subordinate Judge resulted in error in his decision which occasioned failure of Justice. 

 8. We have examined the provisions of Order XXI Rule 52 of the Code. The purport of the Rule is that where any property to be attached is already placed in the Custody of any Court or public officer, the attachment shall be made by a notice to such custody court or officer, requesting that such property may be held subject to the further orders of the Court issuing notice. Provided also that, any question of title or priority arising between the decree-holder and any other person, not being the judgment-debtor, claiming to be interested in such property by virtue of any assignment, attachment or otherwise, shall be determined by such custody Court. Where the property is immovable, further steps prohibiting any transfer of the attached property and proclamation under Order XXI Rule 54 of the Code are to taken. 

 9. From the above facts we find, the Subordinate Judge, First Court by his order dated 22.07.89 practically attached the fixed deposit amounting Taka 92,83,782.20 which was already attached and placed in the custody of the Commercial Court No. 1 in Money Suit No. 91 of 1986. The order was communicated to the said Commercial Court for taking necessary steps. By his order dated 15.03.97 the Subordinate Judge, First Court again requested the Commercial Court No. 1 to take steps in light of his order dated 22.07.89. On further prayer of the petitioner dated 25.03.97, the Subordinate Judge, First Court wrote a letter to the said Commercial Court requesting him to remit the decreetal amount of Taka 58,08,215 out of the fixed deposit. The steps taken and the procedure followed by the Subordinate Judge, First Court, we are afraid, fulfilled the requirements of Order XXI Rule of the Code to make the attachment valid. Because, to effect a valid attachment in respect of the fixed deposit, it was necessary to issue a prior notice under Rule 52 of Order XXI of the Code as the notice is a condition precedent to the order of attachment as is stated in Kanhayalal Hanmantrao v Reginald Mathalone, AIR 1951 Nag 52, and Than Mal v Income Tax. Officer, 67 CWN 916. We could not find any such statutory notice was ever issued by the Subordinate Judge before attaching the fixed deposit which is already in the custody of the Commercial Court No. I by prior attachment. The communication of the order dated 22.07.89 of the Subordinate Judge to the Commercial Court No. 1 is not sanctioned by the Rule.
